competitors.title: Building effective AI agents with Trigger.dev
key_points: Covers 5 Anthropic-inspired agent patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
Uses Trigger.dev tasks with Vercel AI SDK and OpenAI for each pattern
Prompt chaining example: generate marketing copy, validate word count, translate to target language
Routing example: classify question complexity, route to appropriate model (gpt-4o vs gpt-o3-mini)
Parallelization via batch.triggerByTaskAndWait for concurrent LLM calls
Orchestrator-workers pattern: extract claims, verify sources, analyze historical context in parallel
Evaluator-optimizer: recursive translation refinement with quality gates up to 10 iterations
All patterns leverage Trigger.dev's durable execution — no timeouts, automatic retries, checkpointing

competitors.title: Skills: teaching AI agents to act consistently
key_points: Skills are portable instruction sets (SKILL.md) that teach AI coding assistants how to use Trigger.dev
Three-step agent process: Scan (read name/description), Match (check relevance), Load (full instructions)
Skills use open Agent Skills standard — works across Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex CLI
56% of skills not triggered reliably in some orgs — recommends combining with AGENTS.md for reliability
Security warning: malicious HTML comments in SKILL.md can inject hidden instructions
Skills are architectural primitive for reliable, repeatable LLM behavior
Trigger.dev ships 4 skills: authoring-tasks, realtime-and-frontend, authoring-chat-agent, chat-agent-advanced

competitors.title: Trigger.dev Building with AI — Skills, MCP Server, and Context Snippets
key_points: Skills teach patterns; MCP Server enables live project interaction (deploy, trigger, monitor)
Project-level context snippets for CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules/*.md, copilot-instructions.md
llms.txt and llms-full.txt published for LLM consumption
Common mistakes: importing from @trigger.dev/sdk/v3, using deprecated client.defineJob(), wrapping triggerAndWait in Promise.all
Schema validation with schemaTask + Zod for typed payloads
Waits: wait.for (delay), wait.until (date), wait.forToken (external callback)

competitors.title: Trigger.dev AI Agents — chat.agent Durable Multi-Turn Chats
key_points: chat.agent runs every conversation as a single long-lived Trigger.dev task
Survives page refreshes, deploys, idle gaps, and crashes — same in-memory state and workspace
Native Vercel AI SDK support via TriggerChatTransport — no custom protocol
Multi-turn for free: conversation history accumulates server-side, clients only ship new message
Fast cold starts with Head Start — cuts time-to-first-chunk roughly in half
Production primitives: stop generation, steering, edits, branching, sub-agents, HITL approvals, version upgrades
Three primitives: Chat agents (chat.agent()), Sessions (durable channel), Sub-agents (delegation)
